checks: At the nonunit least-active maximum the same-batch central-pair theorem gives a proper full-row cut capturing two central coordinates. The accepted curvature theorem uses those exact signs and the actual normalized section centroid.

The proper normalized threshold theorem gives local C² regularity and the corrected Hessian. Positive homogeneity rescales the Hessian at a positive row by inverse threshold. Multiplication by the strictly positive row weight preserves the positive direction.

The global least-active hypothesis and finiteness and positive homogeneity of all row functions meet the funded-index theorem. One positive direction adds one to the count, and every full row supplies a direction in the all-central case, giving k+f≤d+1.
The excluded full-cut unit-vector case described in the source agrees with the accepted classification. It is outside the theorem hypotheses and contributes no step to the index argument.

dependencies.hypotheses: The positive-weight least-active global maximum is a local maximum and has a strictly positive row and nonunit capacity vector, exactly the conditions for the supplied proper full-row central pair. This frozen predecessor requires independent approval.
Normalize the positive proper threshold to one. The selected two strictly captured coordinates are central in the actual section centroid; its corrected Hessian has the required positive line.

The optimization and fewest nonzero rows assumptions match. Weighted row functions are homogeneous and finite, and each selected full row is C² with one positively curved line. Thus the theorem applies to one selected row or all full rows.

Ensures C² optimized capacity for proper positive rows and at least two strictly captured vertices; in the all-central common centroid case every full row therefore satisfies the corrected curvature hypothesis.

overlap.comparison: Already gives a conditional funded bound from supplied negative tangent cap Hessian spaces. The reviewed theorem selects an eligible full row at an arbitrary nonunit least-active maximum using the central-pair input, and derives the stated row counts.
Provides the general abstract positive-index inequality when positive subspaces are supplied. It does not ensure any such space from the presence of a full row alone.
Classifies a full-cut minimizing row at a local stochastic maximum and realizes its unit-vector capacities; it does not prove the index obstruction under the nonunit assumption.

readability: For an identically zero row, finiteness follows directly by letting a positive threshold decrease to zero. This harmless endpoint is implicit in the capacity definition.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate

source_bindings.locator: Statement and §3, full active rank and proportional funding

summary: The selected central pair furnishes actual positive optimized-capacity curvature. The funded index theorem excludes full active rank and also yields the joint count under the all-central centroid condition.
